resources.string: Saves your list and settings to a file. Tokens never go in, and neither does a request header that could hold a key.
GitHub release digest, as the hubproxy %1$s passed it on

Every request to GitHub goes to this host. It sees each one and can change what comes back: the releases, their digests and the files. Apps you have stay held to their certificate, but a first install through it trusts the hubproxy as much as GitHub, and certificate pinning does not reach it. No token is sent through it, so private projects and GitHub Actions cannot be followed this way.
Check only on Wi-Fi
Background checks wait for Wi-Fi or a cable, so they use no mobile data.
Check only while charging
Background checks wait until the device is charging.
An update that would install by itself waits for Wi-Fi or a cable, as in Obtainium.
An update that would install by itself waits until the device is charging.
The source named version code %2$d, but this file is %1$d, older than the one installed. It is not put over the newer one.
Let Me Downgrade is installed, so Android may put an older version over a newer one. Tern does it only for a release you pick from an app\'s history, never in the background or with Update all.
Take the highest version, as Tern 0.1.0 did

Offers the link with the highest version on the page, whatever its place, and runs the version pattern over the version read from each link. Off reads the page the way Obtainium does: the last link in order is the latest.
An app you uninstall outside Tern leaves the list as well. An archived app stays. Added again from the same place, an app is held to the certificate it had; removing it in Tern forgets that.
Check for updates now?
A link asked Tern to check %1$s for updates. Its source is asked, and nothing is installed.

resources.string: Check
Not now
%1$s was not ready, so Android\'s installer was used for this one.
F-Droid installed this copy, so Tern follows its entry there: updates are the builds F-Droid made and checked, as the F-Droid app gets them.
Follow GitHub releases instead
Updates come from GitHub as soon as they are published, before F-Droid has built and checked them. This skips F-Droid\'s checks. Tern still checks each file and holds it to its own certificate.
